description: Initial verified system knowledge corpus for TESTIMONIUM Caloy AI assistant (CP6)

sources.title: Document Request Submission and Types
sources.sourceText: Parishioners request supported sacramental and canonical documents through TESTIMONIUM by selecting the issuing parish, document type, registrant details, relationship, and purpose. The requester must have an effectively verified Government ID on their TESTIMONIUM profile. For Self, that verified profile ID satisfies the identity requirement and no additional registrant ID upload is needed; the registrant name must satisfy backend Self-name validation. Every non-Self request additionally requires a signed Authorization Letter and separate front and back images of the registrant's valid Government ID.

chunks.content: To create a supported document request, select the issuing parish and document type, then provide the registrant's name, relationship to the requester, relevant sacrament details, and purpose.

All requesters need an effectively verified TESTIMONIUM profile ID. Self reuses that verification and uploads no separate registrant ID. Every non-Self request also needs a signed Authorization Letter and front and back images of the registrant's valid Government ID.

sources.title: Document Request Status Lifecycle
sources.sourceText: After a document request is submitted in TESTIMONIUM, it enters the SUBMITTED status awaiting staff review. Once parish staff begins processing the records, the status moves to PROCESSING. When the certificate is prepared and signed, the status updates to READY_FOR_PICKUP, and the parishioner receives an email notification. If information is incomplete or records cannot be located, the request may be marked REJECTED with an explanatory note. Once claimed at the parish office, the status is marked COMPLETED.

chunks.content: A document request progresses through standard stages: SUBMITTED (received and awaiting review), PROCESSING (parish staff verifying records and preparing certificate), and READY_FOR_PICKUP (signed certificate available at the parish office).

If records are missing or requirements are not met, parish staff may mark the request as REJECTED with specific remarks. When the certificate is claimed in person, the transaction is marked COMPLETED.

sources.title: Payment Proof Upload and Manual Staff Verification
sources.sourceText: For parishes that require handling fees or donations for certificate processing, TESTIMONIUM allows parishioners to upload payment receipts or transaction screenshots (such as GCash or bank transfers). TESTIMONIUM uses OCR to pre-populate transaction references, but all payment proofs must be manually reviewed and verified by parish staff. Payment verification is not instantaneous or automated; staff confirms receipt of funds before documents are released.

chunks.content: When a payment receipt or bank transfer screenshot is uploaded, TESTIMONIUM scans the receipt using OCR to assist with reference identification. However, all payments require manual inspection and approval by parish staff.

Payment verification is not automated or instant. Parish staff reviews the submitted proof against their records before finalizing the transaction. Parishioners should allow standard office processing time for payment validation.

sources.title: Authorization Letter for Representative Requests
sources.sourceText: For a Self request, the parishioner requests their own sacramental document, uses the Government ID already verified through their TESTIMONIUM profile, and does not upload an Authorization Letter or separate registrant ID images. The registrant name must match the verified profile name under the system's conservative name-validation rules. Every non-Self relationship (Parent, Child, Spouse, Sibling, Other Relative, or Authorized Representative) requires a signed Authorization Letter plus clear front and back images of the registrant's valid Government ID. The registrant is the person whose sacramental record is requested; these images are separate from the requester's verified profile ID. For a minor, deceased registrant, or anyone unable to provide the required ID or letter, contact the parish office; TESTIMONIUM does not apply an automatic exemption. OCR only assists staff review and does not verify identity or approve a request.

chunks.content: A Self request uses the requester's existing verified TESTIMONIUM profile ID. It requires no Authorization Letter or separate registrant ID upload, but the registrant name must satisfy backend Self-name validation.

Every non-Self relationship requires a signed Authorization Letter and front and back images of the registrant's valid Government ID. The registrant is the person whose sacramental record is requested, and their evidence is separate from the requester's verified profile ID.

There are no automatic minor, deceased-person, parent, or guardian exemptions. If the required registrant ID or Authorization Letter cannot be provided, contact the parish office. OCR is advisory for staff review and never verifies or approves identity.

sources.title: Scheduling Sacramental Events
sources.sourceText: Parishioners can schedule sacramental events such as Weddings, Baptisms, Funerals, and Blessings through the TESTIMONIUM schedule module. The parishioner selects the parish, chooses the sacramental service, and selects an available calendar slot. The booking is submitted to the parish office for review and approval. Bookings remain tentative until officially confirmed by parish staff.

chunks.content: Parishioners can request sacramental appointments (such as Baptisms, Weddings, Funerals, and Blessings) through the TESTIMONIUM scheduling module by selecting the parish, sacrament type, and preferred available date and time slot.
Submitted schedule requests are tentative bookings that require official review and confirmation by the parish office. A schedule booking is only confirmed once approved by parish staff.

sources.title: Requested and Preferred Priest Policy
sources.sourceText: When scheduling a sacramental event in TESTIMONIUM, parishioners may indicate a preferred or requested priest to preside over the ceremony. However, selecting a preferred priest is a request only and is subject to the priest's schedule, health, parish duties, and official parish assignment. The parish office reserves the right to confirm or reassign the celebrant according to clergy availability.

chunks.content: Parishioners may specify a preferred priest when booking a sacramental service. Selecting a preferred priest is a preference only and cannot be guaranteed. Final celebrant assignment depends on clergy schedule and parish office confirmation.

sources.title: Schedule Rescheduling and Alternative Slot Proposals
sources.sourceText: If a requested date or time for a sacramental event conflicts with parish liturgical schedules or clergy availability, parish staff may propose an alternative date and time. The parishioner receives notification of the proposed reschedule and can review the new schedule slot in their TESTIMONIUM dashboard, where they may accept or decline the proposal.

chunks.content: If a requested schedule slot cannot be accommodated, parish staff can propose an alternative date and time slot. Parishioners can review the proposed change in their dashboard and choose to accept or decline the alternative.

sources.title: Parish Directory and Diocesan Parish Selection
sources.sourceText: TESTIMONIUM provides a diocesan parish directory where parishioners can view information about all member parishes, including address, contact details, and patron saint. Parishioners are not locked to a single parish; users can request certificates or schedule events at any parish within the diocese where their records or sacraments belong.

chunks.content: The TESTIMONIUM parish directory allows parishioners to search and browse all Catholic parishes within the diocese, viewing parish locations, contact details, and patron saint information.
Parishioners are not restricted to their home parish. Users may submit document requests or schedule sacramental celebrations at any parish within the diocese as appropriate for their records.

sources.title: Account Dashboard and Email Notifications
sources.sourceText: Parishioners can manage their TESTIMONIUM account profile, update contact information, and review their history of document requests and sacramental bookings from the personal dashboard. TESTIMONIUM sends transactional email updates when a request status changes, provided email notifications are active on the account.

chunks.content: From the personal dashboard, parishioners can view the status history of all submitted document requests and sacramental appointments, and update their personal profile details.
TESTIMONIUM sends automatic transactional email updates when requests are approved, ready for pickup, or rescheduled. Parishioners should ensure their account email address is accurate.

sources.title: Caloy Virtual Assistant Capabilities and Operational Limitations
sources.sourceText: Caloy is the AI assistant for TESTIMONIUM designed to provide guidance on platform procedures, document request workflows, and scheduling steps. Caloy does NOT have access to private database records, live request tracking, personal payment statuses, or internal parish office records. Caloy cannot modify bookings, verify payments, or issue certificates. For questions regarding personal request status or urgent parish matters, parishioners should contact their parish office directly.
sources.sourceReference: Caloy Virtual Assistant Scope and Boundaries

chunks.content: Caloy provides general guidance on TESTIMONIUM procedures, document request guidelines, and scheduling workflows. Caloy has NO access to live personal database records, individual request tracking statuses, or specific payment verification results.

Caloy cannot look up personal transaction statuses, approve requests, or modify appointments. For specific status inquiries about an ongoing request, parishioners should check their dashboard or contact the issuing parish office directly.
